body.statement:
There is an input-computable integer \(A_{\mathfrak G}\ge1\) with the following property.  For every integer \(j\ge1\), the safe-sector geometry and inductive shared-trace construction determine a finite class \(\mathfrak H_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of rational globally meshed rules, independently of \(K\), such that every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\) has a member \(Q_j\in\mathfrak H_{\mathfrak G,j}\) satisfying
\[
 \inf_{v\in V}\inf_{h\in D_v}P_h\{v\in Q_j(W)\}
 \ge1-\eta-\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2},
\]
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_r}E_h\ell\{Q_j(W)\}
 \le R_r(K)+D\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2},
 \qquad
 \rho_{\mathrm{led}}(Q_j)\le\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}.
\]
If \(j\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}\), the rational global mixture
\[
 Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}}=(1-j^{-1})Q_j+j^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{V\}}
\]
has coverage at least \(1-\eta\), risk at most
\[
 R_r(K)+D\left(\frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}+\frac1j\right),
\]
and total repaired ledger at most \(A_{\mathfrak G}/j^2+1/j\).
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: covariance-orthogonal safe averaging, slowly varying convex gluing, and exhaustive rational finite elements.}

Fix \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\) and \(s>0\).  For the coverage functional
\(f_v(A)=\mathbf 1\{v\in A\}\), the honesty of \(K\) and
\(\mathrm{lem:gaussian\mbox{-}smoothing}\) give, for \(h\in D_v\),
\[
 E_hF_{q_s}^{f_v}(W)\ge1-\eta-\epsilon_s,
 \qquad
 \epsilon_s=\min\{1,s^2\sqrt{d/8}\}.
\tag{20}
\]
For \(f=\ell\), the same lemma gives, for \(h\in H_r\),
\[
 E_hF_{q_s}^{\ell}(W)\le R_r(K)+D\epsilon_s.
\tag{21}
\]

Consider an outer chart \(\alpha\).  In whitened coordinates the normal and tangential Gaussian components in
\(\mathrm{def:inductive\mbox{-}shared\mbox{-}trace\mbox{-}extension}\) are independent.  Fubini's theorem therefore gives, for every bounded action functional \(f\),
\[
 E_hF_{q_\alpha^\circ}^{f}(W)
 =\frac1{|H_{\alpha,L}|}
 \int_{H_{\alpha,L}}
 E_{\varsigma_\alpha(\pi_\alpha h)+t}
 F_{q_s}^{f}(W)\,dt.
\tag{22}
\]
If \(h\in D_v\) and chart \(\alpha\) is active at \(h\), the first inclusion in
\(\mathrm{lem:computable\mbox{-}safe\mbox{-}recession\mbox{-}sectors}\) puts every mean on the right of (22) in \(D_v\).  If \(h\in H_r\), its second inclusion puts every such mean in \(H_r\).  Hence (20)--(22) prove the same coverage and risk bounds for every chart candidate active at \(h\).  On a completed equality face this argument applies to every incident label; no boundary label is discarded.  The product representation and incidence-path independence of the box average are exactly those proved in \(\mathrm{lem:common\mbox{-}ray\mbox{-}folner\mbox{-}coherence}\).  The finite tangential approximation error, when the conditional Gaussian average in (22) is replaced by a finite chart average, is bounded by \(\mathrm{lem:single\mbox{-}chart\mbox{-}averaging}\) and is charged below.

Let \(\{\mu_a\}\) denote all the core, incidence, and internal collar weights used by the extension.  At each point they are nonnegative and sum to one.  For any \([0,R_f]\)-valued functional,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_hF_{\widehat q}^{f}(W)
 &=\sum_a\mu_a(h)E_hF_{q_a}^{f}(W)\\
 &\quad+E_h\sum_a\{\mu_a(W)-\mu_a(h)\}F_{q_a}^{f}(W).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
The coefficients in the last sum add to zero.  The range bound therefore implies
\[
 \left|E_h\sum_a\{\mu_a(W)-\mu_a(h)\}F_{q_a}^{f}(W)\right|
 \le\frac{R_f}{2}E_h\sum_a|\mu_a(W)-\mu_a(h)|.
\tag{24}
\]
Every term with \(\mu_a(h)>0\) is safe by (20)--(22); terms with zero mean weight enter only the remainder (24).  The slow-collar lemma bounds (24), uniformly in \(h\), by \(C_{\mathfrak G}R_fd/(2L)\).  Its second inequality and the established weighted-gluing inequality simultaneously bound the complete path ledger.  Thus data-dependent chart selection introduces no uncharged boundary-honesty or risk step.

It remains to make the rule finite and rational.  The core is bounded.  Every outer candidate is a function only of its bounded normal base \(B_\alpha\); all unbounded tangential coordinates were integrated out in (22).  Gaussian smoothing gives the global \(\ell_1\)-Lipschitz bound \(s^{-1}\sqrt{2/\pi}\), and averaging is a contraction.  The only additional derivative is the cutoff derivative bounded in (17).  The exact rational geometry therefore computes an outward rational Lipschitz constant \(H_{\mathfrak G,j}\) on every bounded chart.  Triangulate all normal bases on one rational mesh of diameter at most
\[
 \delta_j\le \frac{1}{j^2H_{\mathfrak G,j}},
\tag{25}
\]
using one vertex on each common face.  At every vertex, approximate the action-probability vector by a rational simplex vector within \(j^{-2}\) after allocating this tolerance over the finite vertices.  Affine interpolation stays in the probability simplex and, by (25), changes every \([0,R_f]\)-expectation by at most a computable multiple of \(R_fj^{-2}\).  Enumerating all rational simplex assignments at that denominator produces a finite class independent of \(K\), and the simultaneous nearest assignment to the candidates constructed from this particular \(K\) is one member of it.  Shared vertices are rounded once, so exact traces survive rationalization.

Choose
\[
 s_j=j^{-1},\qquad L_j=j^2,\qquad B_j=j,
\tag{26}
\]
use recession refinement parameter \(j^{-1}\), and allocate at most \(j^{-2}\) in total to tangential averaging, finite elements, Gaussian integration, covariance enclosures, and rational rounding.  The smoothing term obeys \(\epsilon_{s_j}\le d/j^2\).  Equations (18)--(19), (25), and the finite allocation just described show that a computable integer \(A_{\mathfrak G}\) can be chosen to dominate, after normalization of the risk entries by the positive number \(D\), every chart, seam, protected-neighborhood, tail, covariance, integration, and rounding charge:
\[
 e_j\le \frac{A_{\mathfrak G}}{j^2}.
\tag{27}
\]
The safe-sector threshold \(R_0(j^{-1})\) and the physical collar lengths may grow arbitrarily fast with \(j\); they are finite computable geometry outputs and do not alter (27).  This proves all three unrepaired inequalities in the statement.

Finally suppose \(j\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}\), put \(\alpha=j^{-1}\), and mix with the deterministic full-set action.  From (27),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_h\{v\in Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}}(W)\}
 &\ge(1-\alpha)(1-\eta-e_j)+\alpha\\
 &=1-\eta-e_j+\alpha(\eta+e_j)\\
 &\ge1-\eta,
 \end{aligned}
\tag{28}
\]
because \(\alpha\eta\ge A_{\mathfrak G}/j^2\ge e_j\).  Since \(0\le R_r(K)\) and \(\ell(V)\le D\),
\[
 R_r(Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}})
 \le(1-\alpha)\{R_r(K)+De_j\}+\alpha D
 \le R_r(K)+D(e_j+\alpha).
\tag{29}
\]
Charging the same global mixture probability in the ledger gives
\(\rho_{\mathrm{led}}(Q_j^{\mathrm{rep}})\le e_j+\alpha\).  Equations (27)--(29) prove the repaired conclusions.
body.justification: It converts the geometric and trace certificates into finite rational rules with an explicit \(j^{-2}\) approximation ledger and a rational exact-honesty repair.
body.gap: Closed by covariance-orthogonal safe averaging, slow-weight variation, and exhaustive shared-vertex rational finite elements.
body.consumer: The effective compatible-density theorem diagonalizes these finite classes and adds the repair term \(j^{-1}\) to the modulus.
